parsed.elsewhere_quote: Since $S_0 = \emptyset$, the function $g$ never takes the value $0$.  Together with §3 this forces $g(x) \equiv c$ for the positive constant $c$.  Thus $f(x) = x + c$
parsed.explanation: Literally the enumeration (i) g≡0 / (ii) V⊆{0,c} with both values attained omits V={c}, c>0, so the objection's local reading is right. But that omitted case is exactly the desired conclusion, and §7 states the general inference used for it: g never takes 0 plus at most one positive value (§3) forces g≡c, and the final boxed answer f(x)=x+c, c≥0, covers it. No case of the necessity conclusion is left unproved; the only repair is deleting the clause "with both values attainable" (or adding one sentence 'if 0∉V we are done').
